stories.title: Food delivery time
stories.day1: Hi, I'm Maya. We run food delivery in Lisbon and want to show customers how long their order will take. The prediction is made the moment the customer places the order, before any courier is assigned. The thing to predict is delivery_minutes: the minutes from the order being placed to the food at the door. Each row is one order, and the answer is in minutes.

facts.text: Prediction made: the moment the customer places the order, before any courier is assigned.
Outcome predicted: delivery_minutes, the minutes from the order being placed to the food at the door.
Unit and horizon: one row per order; the answer is in minutes.

stories.title: Mobile customers leaving
stories.day1: Hello, Omar here, from a mobile operator. We want to know which customers will leave so the retention team can call them. We make the prediction on the first day of each month, using only what we know on that day. The outcome is churned_90d, whether the customer cancels. One row is one customer in one month, and we look at cancelling within the next 90 days.

facts.text: Prediction made: on the first day of each month, using only what is known on that day.
Outcome predicted: churned_90d, whether the customer cancels.
Unit and horizon: one row per customer per month; cancelling within the next 90 days.

stories.day2: Hi again. Please start building the model.

stories.title: Bike share demand
stories.day1: I'm Lena, I plan the bike trucks for our city bike share. We decide at 6 pm the evening before where to move bikes, so that is when the prediction is made. We want to predict bikes_rented, the number of bikes rented. One row is one station for one hour, and we need every hour of the next day.

facts.text: Prediction made: at 6 pm the evening before, to plan the bike trucks for the next day.
Outcome predicted: bikes_rented, the number of bikes rented.
Unit and horizon: one row per station per hour, for every hour of the next day.

facts.text: Prediction made: when the loan application is approved, before any money is paid out.

facts.text: Prediction made: two days before the appointment, when the team decides who gets a reminder call.
Outcome predicted: no_show, whether the patient misses the appointment.

stories.title: Weekly store sales
stories.day1: Tom from a grocery chain. We order stock for each store every Sunday night, before the week starts, and that is when we need the forecast. We predict units_sold, the total units a store sells in the week. One row is one store for one week, and we predict one week ahead.

facts.text: Prediction made: on Sunday night, before the week starts, when stock is ordered.
Outcome predicted: units_sold, the total units a store sells in the week.
Unit and horizon: one row per store per week; one week ahead.

stories.title: Machine breakdowns
stories.day1: I'm Ana, maintenance lead at a packaging plant. Every night at midnight we look at the sensor readings of the day that just ended, and that is when we want the prediction. The outcome is failure_7d, whether the machine breaks down. One row is one machine on one day, and a breakdown counts if it happens within the next 7 days.

facts.text: Prediction made: every night at midnight, from the sensor readings of the day just ended.
Outcome predicted: failure_7d, whether the machine breaks down.
Unit and horizon: one row per machine per day; a breakdown within the next 7 days.
